skip: Want to skip the chat? Go on, I won't be offended.

tutorial.text: Randy Popping. Forty years of muddy fields and missing headliners. Let's get you through your first festival without either.
You've got £{cash} to play with. Bands, toilets, food and the field all come out of that, so don't blow it on the headliner.
Three stars to chase: make a profit, keep the crowd happy, keep the bands happy. Get two and you're through to next year.
This is your forecast. Change anything and it updates. It's a guess, not a promise, but it's a good guess.
Three slots: opener, support and headliner. Start at the top. It's the headliner that sells the tickets.
This is {band_name}. Acts like this usually go for £{rate_low} to £{rate_high}. Make them an offer and see what comes back.
You've three things to play with: the fee, where they sit on the bill, and their cut of the merch.
A counter. That's a good sign: they want the gig. Meet them part way, or offer a bigger merch cut. Just remember their cut comes out of what you sell.
Signed. Remember what you paid. A happy band plays a better set.
Ah, they've walked. No harm done. Try another act.
Now the opener and support. Cheaper acts, and one of them might be the next big thing.
Now the field. Stage first, then toilets and food. {capacity} people need somewhere to go and something to eat, in that order.
A limiter's cheap insurance. Village folk complain about noise; they always have.
A fair price is £{fair_price}. Go above it and fewer come; go below it and the profit gets thin.
Gates are open. Keep an eye on the bars at the top: the crowd, the bands and your three targets.
There's a queue at the food stall. Get a food van in before tempers fray.
Good. Problems only get bigger the longer you leave them.
No queue at the food stalls. That's what planning buys you.
Your support act is stuck on the A-road. Stretch the opener's set, or fill the gap with music over the speakers.
Not a peep from the village. That limiter's earned its keep.
Someone's complained about the noise. Turn it down and the crowd grumbles; ignore it and you might get fined.
That's your headliner on. This is the bit everyone remembers.
